title: Mapungubwe
summary: Mapungubwe, where the Shashe and Limpopo rivers meet in South Africa, was a trading and farming centre between AD 900 and 1300. Its king lived in a palace on top of the hill, apart from commoners, and gold and ivory were traded through East African ports. Around AD 1300 a drier, cooler period led to decline, and power moved to Great Zimbabwe.

uncertainty.note: SAHRA gives changes "between AD900 and AD1300" and decline "around AD1300"; another page says cities were almost completely abandoned by 1320.

as_recorded.value: Overshadowed by rivals by 1300; almost completely abandoned by 1320
